steps.title: Upstream reusable host improvements and enforce contribution lifecycle
steps.summary: Bring reusable PR delivery tracking, repository freshness, claim readability and import hardening back from attached hosts. Establish upstream provenance, contribution receipts and finish-time checks so generic PMO changes return to this source repository and work is committed, pushed and linked to PRs rather than stranded in worktrees.

risk.notes: The source repository is public. Export reusable tooling only; never copy a managed project's plan, credentials, runtime caches, business contracts or recovery artifacts. Preserve generic host ownership and local UI helpers.

value.why: Keeps PMO improvements available to every managed project and prevents silent divergence and abandoned local work.

tasks: Port generic PR prerequisite/delivery state, repository refresh and grouped claim presentation with generic fixtures and standalone UI imports
Port computed import scanning and canonical readiness checks without HigherEd ownership assumptions
Add upstream provenance and receipts: generic changes need a merged upstream contribution covering current content; host-only exceptions are explicit and reviewed
Add read-only worktree inventory and finish checks for clean committed work, matching pushed head and a PR with explicit delivery state; do not create recovery bundles as normal workflow
Document the upstream-first development loop for every agent and prevent host data from entering distributions or exports
Add repeatable offline tests, self-host validation and CI for the PMO product
acceptance: Generic PR tracking, repository refresh and readable active/historical claims work without any HigherEd package or data
Generic changes in an attached PMO fail contribution checks without valid content-bound upstream evidence; declared host-only paths require an explicit reason
Finish checks detect dirty, unpushed and PR-less work and report review versus verified-main delivery distinctly
Attachment/export excludes managed-project plans, secrets, live data, caches and recovery archives
Standalone tests, build, plan validation and scope checks pass and the implementation is merged to PMO main
steps.notes: Reusable source only: no managed-project plans, business contracts, runtime data, credentials or recovery archives. Attachment uses an allowlist and fresh host templates. Receipts bind host bytes to a merged source PR; adapted semantic equivalence remains a review responsibility. Finish distinguishes pending review from main delivery.

steps.title: Count a PR merged into a stacked base as delivered once its content reached main
steps.summary: The PMO marks a merged PR as verified only when it targeted main and its merge commit is an ancestor of main. A PR merged into a stacked base is never verified, so it stays in the waiting queue as Merged; main verification pending although its content may already be on main. Verify such a PR when its head commit is an ancestor of main, or when a step in the approved plan on main dismisses it with a reviewed reason.

risk.notes: Changes only how a merged PR is classified in the local PR snapshot; it cannot clear an open PR or a prerequisite that is not merged. A supersession needs a reviewed reason in the plan on main. Generic source change: contributed upstream first, then recorded as a receipt (G-033).

value.why: Delivered work stays in the waiting queue, which hides PRs that really need review or merge.

acceptance: A merged PR whose base is not main, and whose head commit is in main, is verified
A merged PR with a head not in main stays pending unless the approved plan on main dismisses it with a reason
An open or closed PR is never verified by this rule
